title: Post-1947 Uprising: Colonial Repression and Nationalist Suppression
reason: Well-documented. Nationalist leaders imprisoned/exiled after the 1947 uprising; MDRM dissolved 1947; leaders sentenced to death/life imprisonment. Repression through early 1950s is confirmed.

title: Loi Cadre Grants Madagascar Internal Autonomy
reason: Confirmed. Loi-cadre enacted June 23, 1956. Tsiranana's Social Democratic Party (PSD) won territorial elections. Provincial assemblies and Grand Council established.

title: Madagascar Votes to Join French Community as Autonomous Republic
reason: Confirmed. September 28, 1958 referendum. Malagasy Republic proclaimed October 14, 1958. Tsiranana headed provisional government.

title: Madagascar Achieves Full Independence from France
reason: Confirmed. Full independence June 26, 1960. Tsiranana as president. No armed conflict.

title: Tsiranana Government Suppresses Political Opposition
reason: Broadly confirmed. Tsiranana progressively restricted opposition and operated as a dominant-party state. Specific details about 1962 as the year of key restrictions are consistent with the historical record.

title: Madagascar Joins Organisation of African Unity
reason: Year is wrong by more than 1 year. The OAU was founded May 25, 1963, and Madagascar signed the charter August 10, 1963. Madagascar was a founding member in 1963, not 1964.

title: Peasant Revolt and Urban Labor Strikes Challenge Tsiranana Rule
reason: Confirmed. April 1971 MONIMA armed uprising in Androy led by Monja Jaona. Government suppressed it harshly (45 killed, 847 detained). Urban strikes and student protests also confirmed.

title: May Revolution Overthrows Tsiranana, Ends First Republic
reason: Confirmed. Mass protests from May 1972. Tsiranana transferred power to General Ramanantsoa. Demands included end of French neocolonial dominance.

title: French Cooperation Accords Renegotiated, Military Expelled
reason: Confirmed. Ramanantsoa government renegotiated the French cooperation accords, expelled French military, and withdrew from the Franc Zone.

title: Malagasization of Education System Implemented
reason: Confirmed. Ramanantsoa government replaced French with Malagasy as primary medium of instruction. Rapid implementation created teacher shortages and quality decline.

title: Ratsiraka Seizes Power and Declares Socialist Revolution
reason: Confirmed. Colonel Ratsimandrava assassinated February 11, 1975 after just 6 days in office. Ratsiraka selected head of state June 15, 1975; confirmed by referendum December 21, 1975. Boky Mena published. Democratic Republic of Madagascar proclaimed.

title: Socialist Nationalizations Sweep Banks and Key Sectors
reason: Confirmed. Ratsiraka nationalized banks, insurance, and key export sectors under his socialist program.

title: Forced Agricultural Cooperatives Cause Rice Production Collapse
reason: Confirmed. Socialist cooperative farming policy implemented. Rice production decline and food shortages are well-documented consequences.

title: First IMF Structural Adjustment Program Forces Liberalization
reason: Confirmed. Madagascar signed its first IMF/World Bank structural adjustment program in the late 1970s requiring liberalization in exchange for emergency loans.

title: Socialist Economic Model Collapses, GDP Contracts Sharply
reason: Confirmed. Madagascar experienced one of sub-Saharan Africa's worst economic performances in this period. GDP per capita fell sharply under combined effects of failed socialist policies and oil price shocks.

title: Export Processing Zone Legislation Attracts Garment Investors
reason: Confirmed. EPZ legislation passed mid-1980s, attracting Asian garment manufacturers. Eventually employed over 100,000 workers.

title: Cyclone Kamisy Kills Over 300 in Northwest Madagascar
reason: Year is wrong by 1 year. Cyclone Kamisy struck April 1984, not 1985. Death toll was approximately 68 overall (not over 300). Hit Mahajanga (Majunga) in northwest — region is correct.

title: National Environment Action Plan Launched with World Bank
reason: Confirmed. Madagascar's National Environment Action Plan launched in partnership with World Bank in the late 1980s, positioning Madagascar as a conservation leader.

title: Pro-Democracy Movement Mounts Mass Protests Against Ratsiraka
reason: Confirmed. Broad pro-democracy movement (Forces Vives) with unions, churches, civil society mobilized from 1990. Massive Antananarivo demonstrations forcing Ratsiraka to negotiate.

title: Bloody Saturday: Presidential Guard Massacres Protesters
reason: Confirmed. August 10, 1991 march on Presidential Palace. Presidential guard fired on crowd. Death toll disputed: government said 11, other sources range 10-130. At least 30 deaths are a reasonable figure. Event fundamentally delegitimized Ratsiraka.

title: New Democratic Constitution Adopted, Third Republic Established
reason: Confirmed. New constitution approved August 1992 referendum. Third Republic established with multi-party democracy.

title: Albert Zafy Wins First Competitive Presidential Election
reason: Confirmed. Zafy won second round February 10, 1993 with 66.74%. First genuine multi-party presidential contest. Judged free and fair.

title: President Zafy Impeached by National Assembly
reason: Confirmed. Zafy impeached July 26, 1996 by National Assembly (99 of 134 deputies in favor). High Constitutional Court upheld September 4, 1996.

title: Ratsiraka Returns to Power with Pro-Market Platform
reason: Confirmed. Ratsiraka won December 1996 election (second round December 29) with 50.7% of vote, took office February 1997.

title: Constitutional Referendum Strengthens Presidential Powers
reason: Confirmed. 1998 constitutional referendum approved strengthening of presidential powers and increased provincial autonomy.

title: Sapphire Rush Near Ilakaka Creates Boom-Town Economy
reason: Confirmed. Ilakaka sapphire rush is well-documented. Madagascar became world's leading sapphire producer. Environmental damage and value capture by intermediaries confirmed.

title: Disputed Election Creates Dual Government and Near Civil Conflict
reason: Confirmed. Disputed December 2001 election. Ravalomanana declared himself president February 2002. General strike, roadblocks, dual-government crisis confirmed.

title: Constitutional Court Rules for Ravalomanana, Ratsiraka Flees to Exile
reason: Confirmed. High Constitutional Court ruled for Ravalomanana. Ratsiraka fled to France. Crisis resolved.

title: Political Crisis Causes 13% GDP Contraction
reason: Confirmed. Real GDP dropped 12.7% in 2002, consistent with the stated ~13% figure.

title: Vanilla Price Crashes from $500 to Below $50 per Kilogram
reason: Confirmed. Vanilla peaked at ~$500/kg around 2003-2004, then collapsed to ~$40/kg by mid-2005 due to synthetic vanillin substitution and improved supply. The year and price range are broadly correct.

title: Durban Vision Commits Madagascar to Tripling Protected Areas
reason: Confirmed. Ravalomanana announced Durban Vision at World Parks Congress. Commitment to triple protected areas from 1.7 million to 6 million hectares confirmed.

title: Ambatovy Nickel and Cobalt Mine Project Announced
reason: Confirmed. Ambatovy project announced, led by Sherritt International. Investment projected over $5 billion. Largest single FDI in Madagascar's history.

title: Daewoo Land Deal Triggers Mass Outrage, Fuels Political Crisis
reason: Confirmed. November 2008 reports of 1.3 million hectare, 99-year lease to Daewoo Logistics. Triggered public outrage and contributed directly to 2009 coup. Deal cancelled by Rajoelina.

title: Military-Backed Coup Installs Rajoelina, Madagascar Suspended from AU
reason: Confirmed. Military transferred power to Rajoelina March 17, 2009. Madagascar suspended from both AU and SADC.

title: US and EU Suspend Hundreds of Millions in Aid After Coup
reason: Confirmed. US and EU suspended aid. AGOA trade preferences withdrawn. Garment sector devastated, factory closures, tens of thousands of jobs lost.

title: Post-Coup Rosewood Logging Crisis Devastates Northern National Parks
reason: Confirmed. Organized illegal rosewood logging operations in Marojejy and Masoala national parks after political collapse. Criminal networks exploited the vacuum; exports to China documented by Global Witness.

title: Garment Sector Collapses After AGOA Withdrawal, 40,000 Jobs Lost
reason: Confirmed. AGOA withdrawal caused garment sector collapse. ~40,000 workers lost jobs. Sector had employed over 100,000 at peak.

title: SADC Roadmap Agreement Charts Path Back to Constitutional Rule
reason: Confirmed. SADC-facilitated roadmap signed September 2011. Outlined path to inclusive transitional government and elections.

title: Presidential Elections Restore Constitutional Rule, End Transition
reason: Confirmed. Hery Rajaonarimampianina won 2013 election. International observers judged it broadly credible. Aid programs resumed.

title: Ambatovy Nickel Mine Begins Commercial Production
reason: Confirmed. Ambatovy reached commercial production January 2013. Nameplate capacity 60,000 tonnes nickel and 5,600 tonnes cobalt annually.

title: Cyclone Enawo Kills 81, Destroys 30% of Vanilla Crop
reason: Confirmed. Enawo struck March 7, 2017 as Category 4 equivalent (winds >225 km/h). 81 fatalities confirmed. ~30% vanilla crop damage confirmed by producers. Strongest storm since Gafilo 2004.

title: Urban Pneumonic Plague Outbreak Kills Over 200, Draws WHO Emergency Response
reason: Confirmed. 2,417 cases and 209 deaths by end of acute phase. Outbreak spread to urban centers. WHO deployed emergency response. 7,122 contacts received prophylactic antibiotics.

title: Presidential Election: Rajoelina Defeats Ravalomanana in Credible Runoff
reason: Confirmed. Rajoelina won December 19, 2018 runoff with 55.7%. Ravalomanana accepted result. Broadly judged credible by international observers.

title: COVID-19 Pandemic Eliminates Tourism Revenue, Government Promotes Unproven Remedy
reason: Confirmed. COVID-19 destroyed tourism revenue. Rajoelina promoted Covid-Organics herbal remedy causing WHO diplomatic controversy. GDP contracted.

title: Cyclone Batsirai Kills 121, Displaces 120,000 on Eastern Coast
reason: Confirmed. Batsirai made landfall February 5, 2022. 121 deaths confirmed. ~112,000 displaced. Fianarantsoa and Toamasina (Atsinanana) regions affected.

title: Rajoelina Re-elected in Opposition-Boycotted Controversial Election
reason: Confirmed. November 2023 election boycotted by major opposition. Rajoelina won 58.9%. French citizenship eligibility dispute confirmed. Low turnout (46.4%). SADC observers expressed concerns.
